newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada Prairie harvest seen complete in two weeks.
newsitem.headline: Canada Prairie harvest seen complete in two weeks.

text.p: Canada's Prairie harvest was expected to be completed in two weeks due to good drying conditions, Pioneer Grain said in its crop report for the week ended October 9.
Good drying weather over northern Alberta allowed harvesting to resume in oilseeds. Harvest of cereal crops was also expected to resume.
British Columbia's Dawson Creek region and Alberta's Peace River Valley had just 15 percent of the crop harvested amid rain delays.
Eighty percent of wheat and oats have been combined, with 50 percent of barley and canola harvested in northeastern Saskatchewan. No combining of flax had taken place.
In north central Saskatchewann, fifty-five percent of barley and canola, 50 percent of wheat, 40 percent of oats and durum and five percent of flax had been combined.
The combining of flax was underway in northwestern Saskatchewan with about 60 percent canola, 55 percent barley, 40 percent of wheat and oats and 30 percent durum harvested.
In southwestern Saskatchewan the harvest was just getting underway after being at a standstill for about three weeks.
Seventy-five percent of wheat and durum, 90 percent of oats and barley and 95 percent of canola were combined.
Manitoba southern areas were reporting that the harvest was completed but the northern area was seeded late and harvest was about 80 percent completed.
